items.title: ClawGym: A Scalable Framework for Building Effective Claw Agents
items.title_zh: ClawGym：构建高效 Claw 智能体的可扩展框架
items.summary: ClawGym is a scalable framework covering the full lifecycle of Claw-style personal agents, with ClawGym-SynData (13.5K filtered tasks synthesized from persona-driven intents and skill-grounded operations), realistic mock workspaces and hybrid verification. The authors train ClawGym-Agents via supervised fine-tuning on black-box rollout trajectories and explore reinforcement learning with sandbox-parallel rollouts, and release ClawGym-Bench, a 200-instance benchmark calibrated by automated filtering and human-LLM review.

items.title: Detecting Clinical Discrepancies in Health Coaching Agents: A Dual-Stream Memory and Reconciliation Architecture
items.title_zh: 双流记忆与对账架构：检测健康教练智能体中的临床差异
items.summary: The paper introduces a Dual-Stream Memory Architecture that keeps a patient's evolving narrative separate from the structured FHIR clinical record, with a Reconciliation Engine that classifies discrepancies by type, severity and involved FHIR resources. Across 26 patients and 675 longitudinal coaching sessions, the engine detected 84.4% of designed clinical discrepancies with 86.7% safety-critical recall, and coupling extraction with reconciliation exposed a 13.6% error cascade traced to clinical details lost during memory extraction.

items.title: Hypencoder Revisited: Reproducibility and Analysis of Non-Linear Scoring for First-Stage Retrieval
items.title_zh: Hypencoder 再审视：首阶段检索中非线性打分的可复现性与分析
items.summary: This reproducibility study confirms that the Hypencoder, which replaces fixed inner-product scoring with a query-specific q-net generated by a hypernetwork, beats a similarly trained bi-encoder in-domain and out-of-domain, and that its efficient search substantially cuts query latency with minimal loss. Hard-task support is partial (wins on DL-Hard and FollowIR but not TREC TOT), a Faiss bi-encoder pipeline remains faster, and the non-linear scoring shows no consistent adversarial-robustness disadvantage.

items.title: Enhancing Linux Privilege Escalation Attack Capabilities of Local LLM Agents
items.title_zh: 提升本地 LLM 智能体的 Linux 提权攻击能力
items.summary: An empirical study distills six failure modes of small local models on Linux privilege escalation and evaluates chain-of-thought prompting, RAG, structured prompting, history compression and reflective analysis as extensions to hackingBuddyGPT. Under a shared harness the techniques raise Llama3.1 8B and Qwen2.5 7B from 8% to 67% with guidance, matching guided GPT-4o, while Llama3.1 70B reaches 83%; ablations attribute the largest contribution to reflection and identify vulnerability discovery, not exploitation, as the main constraint.

items.title: AutoSP: Unlocking Long-Context LLM Training Via Compiler-Based Sequence Parallelism
items.title_zh: AutoSP：基于编译器序列并行释放长上下文 LLM 训练
items.summary: AutoSP is presented as the first automated solution for optimizing LLM training for longer contexts, compiling models and applying automated sequence parallelism plus long-context-aware activation checkpointing. It increases training context by up to 2.7x on NVIDIA hardware and 2.5x on AMD over competitive hand-written baselines at negligible runtime cost.

items.title: Length Value Model: Scalable Value Pretraining for Token-Level Length Modeling
items.title_zh: 长度价值模型：面向 Token 级长度建模的可扩展价值预训练
items.summary: LenVM estimates remaining generation length at every decoding step by formulating length modeling as value estimation with a constant negative reward per generated token, yielding annotation-free dense supervision. On LIFEBench-token it raises Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct's exact-length score from 30.9 to 64.8 in one pass and to 83.6 with LCG, and near 200 tokens on GSM8K it retains about 63% Pass@1 versus 6% under a hard token budget.

items.title: Path-Lock Expert: Separating Reasoning Mode in Hybrid Thinking via Architecture-Level Separation
items.title_zh: Path-Lock Expert：通过架构级分离区分混合思考中的推理模式
items.summary: Path-Lock Expert replaces each decoder layer's single MLP with two semantically locked experts, one for /think and one for /no_think, while sharing attention, embeddings, normalization and the language-model head, and a deterministic control-token router selects one expert path for the whole sequence. On Qwen3-4B it generates 17x fewer reflective tokens (6.01 to 0.35 per answer) and roughly halves output length while raising /no_think accuracy from 35.33% to 44.67% and holding /think performance.
